en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Six Gates, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the Heaven of the Pure Abodes, suspended in mid-air.
He was dwelling in a bodhimanda adorned with the seven kinds of wonderful jewels,
together with an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattvas.
Noble son, if you wish to benefit and bring peace and happiness to sentient beings,
you should receive this Dharma of the Six-Gate Dhāraṇī,
which concerns all the sufferings I have endured while wandering through saṃsāra.
May no sentient beings undergo this suffering together with me.
Whatever wealth, nobility, and worldly pleasures I may receive,
may all sentient beings receive such happiness together with me.
If I have committed any evil deeds and have not yet repented of them beforehand, I shall never speak of the Unsurpassed Dharma.
If I have any karmic activities of Māra, I shall first bring them to awareness.
They never direct their minds toward the unsurpassed Dharma as an object of focus.
All my roots of virtue— both mundane and supramundane— that are vast and encompassed by the various perfections (pāramitās).
May all sentient beings swiftly realize the fruit of unsurpassed wisdom.
Just as I have realized liberation, may all sentient beings likewise attain liberation;
let them not abide in attachment to either saṃsāra or nirvāṇa.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

*cāme cāme* (pronounced with a retroflex *m*), *kṣānte kṣānte*, *vartale vartale*, *suvartale suvartale*, *dṛśe dṛśe jartale jartale*, *jartaravati tithu-vati*, *dharma-vati*, *sarva-kleśa-śodhani*, *viśuddhane*, *sarva-arhat-sodhani*, *mano-viśuddhane svāhā*. If there are sons or daughters of good family who possess pure faith...
If one can recite this six-gate *dhāraṇī* during the six periods of the day and night,
all karmic obstructions belonging to that person will be completely extinguished.
They swiftly awakened to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, when the Bhagavat had finished speaking this sutra,
all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the assembly of devas—
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced, and they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Six Gates*.
